# AGENTS.md

## What this service is

`ecommerce-catalog-service` is the **write side / source of truth** in a CQRS system: it owns
products, categories, and attributes. It exposes Connect-RPC (gRPC-compatible) write and read
APIs, persists to MongoDB, and publishes domain events to Kafka via a **transactional outbox**.
Downstream query services project those events into their own read models — this service never
serves reads on their behalf.

This repo is one module of a larger multi-repo workspace (see the workspace-root `AGENTS.md` one
directory up for cross-repo rules, `go.work`, and the local k3d/Tilt stack). Locally, dependencies
on `ecommerce-commons` and the `*-api` repos resolve through the root `go.work`, so changes in
those repos are visible here immediately with no release/bump.

## Common commands

Run from this directory. `make help` lists everything.

```bash
make run                 # go run ./cmd/main.go (reads configs/ + .env, APP_ENV=standalone)
make build               # binary into bin/, injects VERSION via -ldflags
make test                # all tests, -race + coverage.out
make test-unit           # -short (unit only, no containers)
make test-integration    # -tags=integration (spins up real Mongo via testcontainers)
make test-e2e            # -tags=e2e (full app in-process + Mongo + Redpanda containers)
make lint                # golangci-lint (config .golangci.yml)
make fmt                 # gofmt -s + goimports
make generate-mocks      # mockery v3 (see caveat below)
make vuln-check          # govulncheck
make check-all           # deps + fmt + lint + test + vuln-check (the CI pipeline)
make install-tools       # install golangci-lint, mockery, govulncheck, etc.
```

Run a single test:
```bash
go test ./internal/application/product/ -run TestCreateProduct -v
go test -tags=integration ./internal/infrastructure/outbound/mongo/ -run TestProductRepository -v
```

Integration and e2e tests need Docker (testcontainers). Unit tests do not.

## Architecture

**Hexagonal + CQRS-write + event-driven.** Read `cmd/main.go` first — it is the composition
root and contains no business logic, only `fx.Options` module wiring. It composes the commons,
application, and infrastructure `fxconfig` modules; do not construct components in `main.go`.

Layers (each of the three aggregates — `product`, `category`, `attribute` — repeats this shape):

- **`internal/application/<aggregate>/`** — domain model + use cases. The aggregate file
  (`product.go`) holds the domain struct and its invariants; constructors (`NewProduct`) and
  `Update` validate business rules, while `Reconstruct` rebuilds from persistence **without**
  validation. One file per use case (`create_product.go`, `get_product.go`), each defining a
  `...CommandHandler`/`...QueryHandler` interface + impl. `repository.go` is the **port**
  interface, `errors.go` holds sentinel errors, `event_factory.go` is the event-building port.
- **`internal/infrastructure/inbound/connect/`** — Connect-RPC handlers (the driving adapters).
  `module.go` wires handlers and, importantly, declares **per-procedure permission scopes** in
  `provideProcedurePermissions` (e.g. `products:write`, `categories:read`) enforced by the
  commons validation interceptor.
- **`internal/infrastructure/outbound/mongo/`** — repository implementations (driven adapters).
  Each aggregate has `*_entity.go` (BSON document), `*_mapper.go` (domain↔entity), and
  `*_repository.go`. Repos embed `commonsmongo.GenericRepository` and are built with
  `commonsmongo.NewGenericRepository` plus a tenant-aware collection provider; custom queries like
  `FindList` build `bson` filters on top.
- **`internal/infrastructure/outbound/kafka/`** — event factories that turn domain objects into
  protobuf outbox messages. Topic is resolved via `apiEvents.TopicFor(event)` from the `-api` repo.

### The write path (the core pattern)

A command handler like `createProductHandler.Handle` does: validate cross-aggregate refs →
build the domain object → build an outbox `Message` from the event factory → then
`persistAndPublish` wraps the DB insert **and** `outbox.Create` in a single
`mongo.WithTransaction`. The transactional outbox guarantees the event is durably queued in the
same transaction as the state change; the actual Kafka send (`res.Send(ctx)`) happens
best-effort **after** commit and its error is intentionally ignored (already logged by the outbox
relay). Preserve this ordering when adding new write use cases.

### Multi-tenancy (database-per-tenant)

`main.go` composes `fx_commons.NewCommonsModule()`, which includes the commons tenant module;
the infrastructure module adds tenant-service API adapters. Tenant-scoped collections (`product`,
`category`, `attribute`) use `commonsmongo.NewGenericRepository` with
`commonstenant.NewMultiTenantCollectionProvider`, which resolves a per-tenant database from request
context. The transactional `outbox` collection is **not** tenant-scoped. Respect tenant context in
any new repository query.

## Conventions & gotchas

- **Mocks (`mockery` v3, `make generate-mocks`)** are generated **inline** in each application
  package — the `Repository` and `*EventFactory` mocks live beside their interface as
  `package product`/`category`/`attribute` (not a `mocks/` subpackage). Only the commons
  `Outbox`/`TxManager` mocks land in `internal/testutil/mocks/` (`package mocks`). Regenerate via
  the config rather than hand-editing `mock_*.go`.
- **API contracts live in `ecommerce-catalog-service-api`**, not here. Protobuf under that repo's
  `proto/` (`catalog/v1/` for RPCs, `catalog/events/v1/` for Kafka events) generates the
  `catalogv1connect` handlers and `eventsv1` types this service imports. To change an RPC or
  event schema, edit `.proto` there and `make generate` — never hand-edit `gen/`.
- **MongoDB indexes are declarative migrations** in `db/migrations/*.json` (golang-migrate
  command format). The default runner applies them when `mongo.migrations.enabled`; when
  `multi-tenancy.enabled`, the commons tenant module decorates it to migrate every active tenant.
  Add indexes there.
- **Config** is `configs/config.standalone.yaml` selected by `APP_ENV` (set in `.env`),
  overridable by env vars. Covers `mongo`, `kafka`, `security.jwks` (JWT via JWKS, Logto locally),
  `logger`, `observability` (OpenTelemetry).
- **CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) delegates to the shared `go-ci.yml` in
  `ecommerce-infrastructure`; coverage excludes mocks, `module.go`, `main.go`, and infrastructure
   glue. The workspace OpenCode plugin auto-formats edited `.go` files (see workspace-root
   `AGENTS.md`).

# AGENTS.md

## What this is

`ecommerce-commons` is the shared Go library imported by every service in the ecommerce
workspace (catalog, product-query, category-query, image, tenant). It has **no `cmd/` and no
`main`**. It ships reusable building blocks plus their Fx wiring, which services compose in
their own `cmd/main.go`. There is nothing to "run"; you build, test, and lint it, and consumers
pick up changes locally through the root `go.work` (no tag/release needed for local dev — see the
workspace root `AGENTS.md`).

## Commands

```bash
make test                # all tests: -v -race -coverprofile
make test-unit           # -short (unit only)
make test-integration    # -tags=integration (spins up real deps via testcontainers — needs Docker)
make lint                # golangci-lint (v2; stricter-than-services config in .golangci.yml)
make fmt                 # gofmt -s + goimports
make generate-mocks      # mockery (not currently used)
make vuln-check          # govulncheck (excludes testutil/mocks/test)
make check-all           # deps + fmt + lint + test + vuln-check (the CI pipeline)
make install-tools       # golangci-lint, mockery, govulncheck, go-mod-outdated, go-licenses
```

Run a single test: `go test ./pkg/kafka/consumer/ -run TestRouter -v`
Integration tests are gated behind `-tags=integration`; plain `go test ./...` / `make test-unit` skips them.

## Module system (the core convention)

Runtime packages contain framework-agnostic functionality. Their Fx constructors and options
live in a sibling `fxconfig` package: for example, `pkg/mongo` is wired by
`pkg/mongo/fxconfig`, and configuration loading by `pkg/core/config/fxconfig`. Do not add Fx
imports or DI constructors to runtime packages. Add them to the closest `fxconfig` package.

Each Fx package exposes a constructor returning `fx.Option`, conventionally named
`New*Module()`. `pkg/fxconfig.NewCommonsModule()` aggregates the standard library modules:
core, HTTP, Mongo, observability, Kafka, tenant, client credentials, and JWKS validation.
Services can compose this aggregate or individual `fxconfig` modules; they do not construct
infrastructure components by hand.

Modules load their configuration from koanf through the shared configuration loader. Tests that
compose Fx modules must provide the required configuration through the normal configuration path.

Top-level modules and what they wire:
- `pkg/core/fxconfig` — `NewCoreModule()`: config loading (koanf + dotenv), zap logger, readiness
  health, and 5-minute Fx start/stop timeouts. This is the foundation every service starts with.
- `pkg/kafka/fxconfig` — `NewKafkaModule()`: Kafka configuration, producer, protobuf serde, and
  the outbox pattern. Consumer wiring is opt-in via `pkg/kafka/consumer/fxconfig`.
- `pkg/mongo/fxconfig` — `NewMongoModule()`: Mongo client, database, transaction manager, metric
  views, lifecycle, and the default single-database migration runner.
- `pkg/tenant/fxconfig` — `NewTenantModule()`: multi-tenancy lifecycle, migrations, cleanup worker,
  and Connect-RPC interceptors.
- `pkg/http/fxconfig`, `pkg/observability/fxconfig`, and `pkg/security/*/fxconfig` — transport,
  telemetry, and authentication building blocks.

Config loading is centralized in `config.Load[T]` (`pkg/core/config/loader.go`): each module loads
its own subtree of the service's YAML by key (`"mongo"`, `"kafka"`, etc.).

## Multi-tenancy (database-per-tenant)

Tenant data lives in a **separate Mongo database per tenant**, named `{baseDatabase}_{slug}`.
The slug is resolved per-request from context. This is the single most important cross-cutting
concern to get right in repository code:

- `mongo.NewGenericRepository[Domain, Entity](...)` accepts a `mongo.CollectionProvider`. The
  provider resolves a collection for the request context, so services can supply either a fixed
  collection or tenant-aware collection selection without changing repository code.
- `tenant.NewMultiTenantCollectionProvider(...)` — tenant-aware collection selection. It resolves
  the database from the tenant in request context and is required for tenant-scoped data.
- `mongo.NewStaticCollectionProvider(...)` — fixed collection in the base database, suitable for
  non-tenant data such as the transactional `outbox`.

Choosing the wrong provider silently reads/writes the wrong database, so match it to whether the
data is tenant-scoped. See `pkg/mongo/collection_provider.go` and
`generic_repository.go`.

## Connect-RPC interceptor ordering

Interceptors are collected via the fx group `connect_interceptor` and sorted by an integer
`Priority` (**lower runs earlier**). Because ordering is global across packages, the priorities
are coordinated constants — when adding an interceptor, pick a priority that fits this chain:

```
10 Recovery  15 Tracing  18 Tenant-Resolver  20 Logger  22 Auth
25 Validation  26 Tenant-Validator  30 Timeout  40 RateLimit  50 Bulkhead
```

The named constants live in `pkg/tenant/fxconfig/module.go`
(`ResolverInterceptorPriority=18`, `ValidatorInterceptorPriority=26`) and
`pkg/security/validation/fxconfig/module.go` (`AuthInterceptorPriority=22`). Tracing uses 15 in
`pkg/observability/fxconfig/module.go`; the built-in chain is in
`pkg/http/connect/interceptor/fxconfig/module.go`. Tenant/logger/auth ordering is deliberate:
resolve tenant before logging so the tenant field appears in logs, validate auth after logging so
failures are logged.

## Linting notes

`.golangci.yml` is intentionally strict for a library: `godot` (comments end with a period),
`revive`'s `exported` rule (exported symbols need doc comments), `gocyclo` at complexity 20,
plus `gosec` and `errcheck` with `check-blank`/`check-type-assertions`. Test files relax several
of these. Documentation comments are encouraged for exported symbols but are no longer enforced by CI.

package config

import "time"

// Config represents the main Kafka configuration.
type Config struct {
	Brokers         string          `koanf:"brokers"`          // Comma-separated list of Kafka broker addresses (e.g., "localhost:9092,localhost:9093")
	ConsumersConfig ConsumersConfig `koanf:"consumers-config"` // Global and individual consumer configurations
	ProducerConfig  ProducerConfig  `koanf:"producer-config"`  // Producer-specific configuration
}

// ConsumersConfig holds global default settings and individual consumer configurations.
type ConsumersConfig struct {
	DefaultGroupID           string           `koanf:"default-group-id"`            // Default consumer group ID (applied to consumers without explicit group-id)
	DefaultAutoOffsetReset   string           `koanf:"default-auto-offset-reset"`   // Default offset reset policy: "earliest" or "latest"
	DefaultMaxRetries        *uint            `koanf:"default-max-retries"`         // Default maximum retries for message processing (0-99)
	DefaultInitialBackoff    time.Duration    `koanf:"default-initial-backoff"`     // Default initial backoff duration for retries (100ms-30s)
	DefaultMaxBackoff        time.Duration    `koanf:"default-max-backoff"`         // Default maximum backoff duration for retries (1s-5m)
	DefaultProcessingTimeout time.Duration    `koanf:"default-processing-timeout"`  // Default timeout for processing a single message (1s-10m)
	DefaultChannelBufferSize int              `koanf:"default-channel-buffer-size"` // Default internal message channel buffer size (10-10000)
	DefaultMaxPollRecords    int              `koanf:"default-max-poll-records"`    // Default max records per poll iteration (1-10000)
	ConsumerConfig           []ConsumerConfig `koanf:"consumers"`                   // Individual consumer configurations
}

// ConsumerConfig represents configuration for an individual Kafka consumer.
type ConsumerConfig struct {
	Name                    string        `koanf:"name"`                      // Unique consumer name/identifier (required)

2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"strings"
7		"time"
8	
9		"github.com/Sokol111/ecommerce-commons/pkg/core/health"
10		"github.com/Sokol111/ecommerce-commons/pkg/kafka/config"
11		"github.com/twmb/franz-go/pkg/kadm"
12		"github.com/twmb/franz-go/pkg/kgo"
13		"go.uber.org/fx"
14		"go.uber.org/zap"
15	)
16	
17	func provideConsumerClient(lc fx.Lifecycle, conf config.Config, consumerConf config.ConsumerConfig, log *zap.Logger, componentMgr health.ComponentManager) (*kgo.Client, error) {
18		brokers := strings.Split(conf.Brokers, ",")
19	
20		resetOffset := kgo.NewOffset().AtEnd()
21		if consumerConf.AutoOffsetReset == "earliest" {
22			resetOffset = kgo.NewOffset().AtStart()
23		}
24	
25		opts := []kgo.Opt{
26			kgo.SeedBrokers(brokers...),
27			kgo.ConsumerGroup(consumerConf.GroupID),
28			kgo.ConsumeTopics(consumerConf.Topic),
29			kgo.ConsumeResetOffset(resetOffset),
30			kgo.AutoCommitInterval(3 * time.Second),
31			kgo.AutoCommitMarks(),
32			kgo.OnPartitionsAssigned(func(ctx context.Context, cl *kgo.Client, assigned map[string][]int32) {
33				for topic, parts := range assigned {
34					log.Info("partitions assigned",
35						zap.String("topic", topic),
36						zap.Int("partition_count", len(parts)),
37						zap.Int32s("partitions", parts))
38				}
39			}),
40			kgo.OnPartitionsRevoked(func(ctx context.Context, cl *kgo.Client, revoked map[string][]int32) {
41				for topic, parts := range revoked {
42					log.Info("partitions revoked",
43						zap.String("topic", topic),
44						zap.Int("partition_count", len(parts)),
45						zap.Int32s("partitions", parts))
46				}
47			}),
48			kgo.OnPartitionsLost(func(ctx context.Context, cl *kgo.Client, lost map[string][]int32) {
49				for topic, parts := range lost {
50					log.Warn("partitions lost",
51						zap.String("topic", topic),
52						zap.Int("partition_count", len(parts)),
53						zap.Int32s("partitions", parts))
54				}
55			}),
56		}
57	
58		client, err := kgo.NewClient(opts...)
59		if err != nil {
60			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create kafka consumer, name: %s: %w", consumerConf.Name, err)
61		}
62	
63		componentName := "kafka-consumer-" + consumerConf.Name
64		markReady := componentMgr.AddComponent(componentName)
65	
66		lc.Append(fx.Hook{
67			OnStart: func(ctx context.Context) error {
68				log.Info("subscribing to topic", zap.String("topic", consumerConf.Topic))
69	
70				// Verify topic is available
71				if err := verifyTopicAvailable(ctx, client, consumerConf.Topic, log); err != nil {
72					if consumerConf.FailOnTopicError {
73						return err
74					}
75					log.Warn("topic verification failed, continuing anyway", zap.Error(err))
76				}
77	
78				markReady()
79				return nil
80			},
81			OnStop: func(ctx context.Context) error {
82				log.Info("closing kafka consumer")
83				client.Close()
84				return nil
85			},
86		})
87	
88		return client, nil
89	}
90	
91	// verifyTopicAvailable checks if topic exists and has partitions.
92	func verifyTopicAvailable(ctx context.Context, client *kgo.Client, topic string, log *zap.Logger) error {
93		admClient := kadm.NewClient(client)
94		topics, err := admClient.ListTopics(ctx, topic)
95		if err != nil {
96			return fmt.Errorf("failed to get topic metadata: %w", err)
97		}
98	
99		topicDetail, ok := topics[topic]
100		if !ok {
101			return fmt.Errorf("topic %s not found in metadata", topic)
102		}
103	
104		if topicDetail.Err != nil {
105			return fmt.Errorf("topic %s has error: %w", topic, topicDetail.Err)
106		}
107	
108		if len(topicDetail.Partitions) == 0 {
109			return fmt.Errorf("topic %s has no partitions", topic)
110		}
111	
112		log.Info("topic is ready",
113			zap.String("topic", topic),
114			zap.Int("partitions", len(topicDetail.Partitions)))
115		return nil
116	}

# AGENTS.md

## What this is

`ecommerce-commons` is the shared Go library imported by every service in the ecommerce
workspace (catalog, product-query, category-query, image, tenant). It has **no `cmd/` and no
`main`**. It ships reusable building blocks plus their Fx wiring, which services compose in
their own `cmd/main.go`. There is nothing to "run"; you build, test, and lint it, and consumers
pick up changes locally through the root `go.work` (no tag/release needed for local dev — see the
workspace root `AGENTS.md`).

## Commands

```bash
make test                # all tests: -v -race -coverprofile
make test-unit           # -short (unit only)
make test-integration    # -tags=integration (spins up real deps via testcontainers — needs Docker)
make lint                # golangci-lint (v2; stricter-than-services config in .golangci.yml)
make fmt                 # gofmt -s + goimports
make generate-mocks      # mockery (not currently used)
make vuln-check          # govulncheck (excludes testutil/mocks/test)
make check-all           # deps + fmt + lint + test + vuln-check (the CI pipeline)
make install-tools       # golangci-lint, mockery, govulncheck, go-mod-outdated, go-licenses
```

Run a single test: `go test ./pkg/kafka/consumer/ -run TestRouter -v`
Integration tests are gated behind `-tags=integration`; plain `go test ./...` / `make test-unit` skips them.

## Module system (the core convention)

Runtime packages contain framework-agnostic functionality. Their Fx constructors and options
live in a sibling `fxconfig` package: for example, `pkg/mongo` is wired by
`pkg/mongo/fxconfig`, and configuration loading by `pkg/core/config/fxconfig`. Do not add Fx
imports or DI constructors to runtime packages. Add them to the closest `fxconfig` package.

Each Fx package exposes a constructor returning `fx.Option`, conventionally named
`New*Module()`. `pkg/fxconfig.NewCommonsModule()` aggregates the standard library modules:
core, HTTP, Mongo, observability, Kafka, tenant, client credentials, and JWKS validation.
Services can compose this aggregate or individual `fxconfig` modules; they do not construct
infrastructure components by hand.

Modules load their configuration from koanf through the shared configuration loader. Tests that
compose Fx modules must provide the required configuration through the normal configuration path.

Top-level modules and what they wire:
- `pkg/core/fxconfig` — `NewCoreModule()`: config loading (koanf + dotenv), zap logger, readiness
  health, and 5-minute Fx start/stop timeouts. This is the foundation every service starts with.
- `pkg/kafka/fxconfig` — `NewKafkaModule()`: Kafka configuration, producer, protobuf serde, and
  the outbox pattern. Consumer wiring is opt-in via `pkg/kafka/consumer/fxconfig`.
- `pkg/mongo/fxconfig` — `NewMongoModule()`: Mongo client, database, transaction manager, metric
  views, lifecycle, and the default single-database migration runner.
- `pkg/tenant/fxconfig` — `NewTenantModule()`: multi-tenancy lifecycle, migrations, cleanup worker,
  and Connect-RPC interceptors.
- `pkg/http/fxconfig`, `pkg/observability/fxconfig`, and `pkg/security/*/fxconfig` — transport,
  telemetry, and authentication building blocks.

Config loading is centralized in `config.Load[T]` (`pkg/core/config/loader.go`): each module loads
its own subtree of the service's YAML by key (`"mongo"`, `"kafka"`, etc.).

## Multi-tenancy (database-per-tenant)

Tenant data lives in a **separate Mongo database per tenant**, named `{baseDatabase}_{slug}`.
The slug is resolved per-request from context. This is the single most important cross-cutting
concern to get right in repository code:

- `mongo.NewGenericRepository[Domain, Entity](...)` accepts a `mongo.CollectionProvider`. The
  provider resolves a collection for the request context, so services can supply either a fixed
  collection or tenant-aware collection selection without changing repository code.
- `tenant.NewMultiTenantCollectionProvider(...)` — tenant-aware collection selection. It resolves
  the database from the tenant in request context and is required for tenant-scoped data.
- `mongo.NewStaticCollectionProvider(...)` — fixed collection in the base database, suitable for
  non-tenant data such as the transactional `outbox`.

Choosing the wrong provider silently reads/writes the wrong database, so match it to whether the
data is tenant-scoped. See `pkg/mongo/collection_provider.go` and
`generic_repository.go`.

## Connect-RPC interceptor ordering

Interceptors are collected via the fx group `connect_interceptor` and sorted by an integer
`Priority` (**lower runs earlier**). Because ordering is global across packages, the priorities
are coordinated constants — when adding an interceptor, pick a priority that fits this chain:

```
10 Recovery  15 Tracing  18 Tenant-Resolver  20 Logger  22 Auth
25 Validation  26 Tenant-Validator  30 Timeout  40 RateLimit  50 Bulkhead
```

The named constants live in `pkg/tenant/fxconfig/module.go`
(`ResolverInterceptorPriority=18`, `ValidatorInterceptorPriority=26`) and
`pkg/security/validation/fxconfig/module.go` (`AuthInterceptorPriority=22`). Tracing uses 15 in
`pkg/observability/fxconfig/module.go`; the built-in chain is in
`pkg/http/connect/interceptor/fxconfig/module.go`. Tenant/logger/auth ordering is deliberate:
resolve tenant before logging so the tenant field appears in logs, validate auth after logging so
failures are logged.

## Linting notes

`.golangci.yml` is intentionally strict for a library: `godot` (comments end with a period),
`revive`'s `exported` rule (exported symbols need doc comments), `gocyclo` at complexity 20,
plus `gosec` and `errcheck` with `check-blank`/`check-type-assertions`. Test files relax several
of these. Documentation comments are encouraged for exported symbols but are no longer enforced by CI.

go.work
    30	
    31	- **Go microservices** — tied together by the root `go.work` (Go 1.26.4 workspace).
    32	- **Nuxt/TypeScript UIs** — each a standalone `pnpm` project.
    33	
    34	Because subdirectories are separate repos, **commit and branch per-repo**. A change touching a
    35	service and its API contract is usually two commits in two repos.
    36	
    37	## Component map
    38	
    39	| Repository | Kind | Responsibility |
    40	|---|---|---|
    41	| [`ecommerce-catalog-service`](https://github.com/Sokol111/ecommerce-catalog-service) (+ [`-api`](https://github.com/Sokol111/ecommerce-catalog-service-api)) | Go service | Write side / source of truth for products, categories, attributes. Emits domain events to Kafka. |
    42	| [`ecommerce-product-query-service`](https://github.com/Sokol111/ecommerce-product-query-service) (+ [`-api`](https://github.com/Sokol111/ecommerce-product-query-service-api)) | Go service | CQRS read model for products, built from catalog Kafka events. |
    43	| [`ecommerce-category-query-service`](https://github.com/Sokol111/ecommerce-category-query-service) (+ [`-api`](https://github.com/Sokol111/ecommerce-category-query-service-api)) | Go service | CQRS read model for categories. |
    44	| [`ecommerce-image-service`](https://github.com/Sokol111/ecommerce-image-service) (+ [`-api`](https://github.com/Sokol111/ecommerce-image-service-api)) | Go service | Image upload/serving (MinIO + imgproxy). |
    45	| [`ecommerce-tenant-service`](https://github.com/Sokol111/ecommerce-tenant-service) (+ [`-api`](https://github.com/Sokol111/ecommerce-tenant-service-api)) | Go service | Multi-tenancy; consumed by every other service. |
    46	| [`ecommerce-commons`](https://github.com/Sokol111/ecommerce-commons) | Go library | Shared modules: `core`, `http`, `kafka`, `observability`, `mongo`, `security`, `tenant`, `testutil`. |
    47	| [`ecommerce-infrastructure`](https://github.com/Sokol111/ecommerce-infrastructure) | Tooling | Deployment for both environments: local dev stack (k3d + Tilt + docker-compose) and production (k3s), plus shared Helm charts and seeders. |
    48	| [`ecommerce-ui`](https://github.com/Sokol111/ecommerce-ui) | Nuxt UI | Storefront. |
    49	| [`ecommerce-admin-ui`](https://github.com/Sokol111/ecommerce-admin-ui) | Nuxt UI | Admin console. |
    50	| [`ecommerce-platform-ui`](https://github.com/Sokol111/ecommerce-platform-ui) | Nuxt UI | Platform console. |
    51	
    52	Each `*-api` repo holds the protobuf contract for its service: RPCs under `<name>/v1/` and
    53	Kafka event schemas under `<name>/events/v1/`, with generated Go and TypeScript clients.
    54	
    55	## Architecture
    56	
    57	- **CQRS + event-driven.** The catalog service owns all writes and publishes events to Kafka.
    58	  Query services consume those events into their own MongoDB read models — they never call the
    59	  catalog service synchronously for data they should be projecting.
    60	- **Hexagonal Go services.** `cmd/main.go` is the composition root; `internal/application/`
    61	  holds domain + use cases; `internal/infrastructure/{inbound,outbound}/` holds adapters
    62	  (Connect-RPC/gRPC, Kafka, MongoDB).
    63	- **Dependency injection** via [`go.uber.org/fx`](https://github.com/uber-go/fx) modules.
    64	- **API contracts** are protobuf, generated with [`buf`](https://buf.build) — edit `.proto`
    65	  and regenerate; never hand-edit `gen/`.
    66	- **Multi-tenant SaaS.** Self-service sign-up provisions a new store per tenant. Tenancy is
    67	  pervasive — tenant context flows through every request, and each tenant's data is isolated in
    68	  its own dedicated database (named with the tenant slug, `*_<tenant-slug>`).
    69	- **Auth** is JWT validated against a JWKS endpoint (Logto).
    70	- **Observability** via OpenTelemetry (Grafana/Prometheus/Tempo stack).
    71	
    72	See [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) for the full architecture deep-dive.
    73	
    74	## Architecture diagrams
    75	
    76	- [Store Lifecycle](docs/architecture/platform-overview.md) — portfolio-level overview of tenant
    77	  provisioning, catalog management, and the event-driven storefront.
    78	- [Product Update Flow](docs/architecture/product-update-flow.md) — reliable product propagation
    79	  from a catalog write through the transactional outbox to the storefront read model.
    80

I can't write a reliable plan yet, so `plan.json`, `plan.md` and `answers.json` don't exist yet. Here is what the source shows so far.

**Which services move:** `ecommerce-catalog-service` and `ecommerce-image-service`. Everything else stays on Redpanda.

**Topics written from inside the moving group:**
- The catalog service writes `catalog.product.events`, `catalog.category.events` and `catalog.attribute.events` (`src/ecommerce-catalog-service-api/pkg/events/topics.go:11-13`).
- The image service also writes to `catalog.product.events` (`src/ecommerce-image-service-api/pkg/events/topics.go:11-16`).

**Topics read from inside the moving group:**
- Both services read `tenant.tenant.events`, which the tenant service produces outside the group. Both services wire the consumer module (`src/ecommerce-catalog-service/internal/infrastructure/fxconfig/module.go:13`, `src/ecommerce-image-service/internal/infrastructure/fxconfig/module.go:36`). This is an inbound flow from Redpanda to Kafka.
- The image service reads `catalog.product.events`. Both its producer and its consumer move, so this stays inside the group.

**Likely outbound flows (Kafka to Redpanda):** the product and category query services read catalog topics. The docs name only one specific binding: product query reads `catalog.product.events` (`product-update-flow.md:100-110`). Which topics the category query service reads is unconfirmed.

**Open question:** `catalog.product.events` must be on Kafka for the image service and also reach the product query service on Redpanda. The rule against mirroring a topic both ways depends on there being no producer left on Redpanda for that topic. I'm asking the tenant service's repository and the broker to confirm this.

**What I can't see:**
- The deployed Helm values (topic names, group ids, offset settings, dead-letter topics)
- The consumer groups that are actually running
- The other teams' consumer code
- The topic settings on Redpanda

The six requests in `requests.json` cover these:
- **R1:** consumer groups on Redpanda
- **R2–R4:** read access to the product-query, category-query and tenant-service repositories
- **R5:** the deployed Kafka settings from the Helm values
- **R6:** topic settings on Redpanda, and confirmation that the Kafka broker is still empty

Once these are answered I'll write the three files.

# AGENTS.md

## What this service is

`ecommerce-product-query-service` is the **read side of a CQRS split** for products. It owns no
writes to product data: it consumes domain events from Kafka (emitted by the catalog service and
image service) into its own denormalized MongoDB read model, and serves fast product queries over
Connect-RPC. **Never call the catalog service synchronously for data that should be projected from
events** — the projection is the source of truth for reads.

It is one repo inside a larger multi-repo workspace (see the parent `../AGENTS.md`). Its API
contract lives in the separate `ecommerce-product-query-service-api` repo; it consumes event
schemas from `ecommerce-catalog-service-api` and `ecommerce-image-service-api`. Locally these
resolve through the root `go.work`, so cross-repo changes are visible immediately without a
release/bump.

## Commands

```bash
make run                 # go run ./cmd/main.go
make build               # binary into bin/ (injects VERSION via -ldflags)
make test                # all tests, -race + coverage → coverage.out
make test-unit           # -short (unit only)
make test-integration    # -tags=integration (real deps)
make lint                # golangci-lint (config .golangci.yml)
make fmt                 # gofmt -s + goimports
make check-all           # deps + fmt + lint + test + vuln-check (the CI pipeline)
make install-tools       # golangci-lint, mockery, govulncheck, gosec, etc.
```

Run a single test: `go test ./internal/application/productview/ -run TestX -v`

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) delegates to the shared `ecommerce-infrastructure` Go CI workflow.

> Note: there are no `*_test.go` files in the repo yet.

## Architecture

**Hexagonal, wired entirely with `go.uber.org/fx`.** `cmd/main.go` is the composition root — it
only assembles the commons, application, and infrastructure `fxconfig` modules; no business logic
lives there. Do not construct components in `main.go`.

Two aggregates, each a folder under `internal/application/`:
- **`productview/`** — the product read model. Domain type `ProductView` is denormalized and
  read-optimized (unlike the command-side `Product`). Query handlers (`get_*.go`), command handlers
  (`upsert_product.go`, `delete_product.go`, `update_image_urls.go`), and the `Repository` port.
- **`attributeview/`** — master attribute definitions (name, type, options), projected separately
  and joined into products at query time.

### Layers
- `internal/application/<aggregate>/` — domain + use cases. `repository.go` is the port interface;
  handlers are split one-per-file and each defines its own `…QueryHandler` / `…CommandHandler`
  interface + constructor (registered in `application/module.go`).
- `internal/infrastructure/inbound/kafka/` — event consumers (the write path into the read model).
- `internal/infrastructure/inbound/connect/` — Connect-RPC handlers (the read path out).
- `internal/infrastructure/outbound/mongo/` — repository implementations (`*_entity.go` +
  `*_mapper.go` per aggregate).

### Event ingestion (the projection)
`kafka/module.go` registers two consumers via `consumer.RegisterHandlerAndConsumer` and routes each
event type to a handler method:
- `catalog-events` → `ProductUpdatedEvent`, `ProductDeletedEvent` (catalog),
  `ProductImagePromotedEvent` (image service).
- `catalog-attribute-events` → `AttributeUpdatedEvent`.

Two projection subtleties that must be preserved when editing the repo layer:
- **Version-guarded upsert** (`productViewRepository.Upsert`): the filter requires
  `version < event.Version`, so out-of-order/stale events are dropped (a matched/upserted count of 0
  is a logged no-op, not an error).
- **Image URLs are decoupled from product updates.** The image service publishes
  `ProductImagePromoted` only on promotion, not on every product change. `Upsert` therefore
  preserves existing `smallImageUrl`/`largeImageUrl` when `imageId` is unchanged (Mongo
  `$mergeObjects` pipeline), and `UpdateImageURLs` only writes when the stored `imageId` still
  matches — so an image event arriving before or after a product event never clobbers correct data.

### Read/query path
Connect handlers (`connect/product_handler.go`) translate proto ↔ domain and **join at read time**:
stored `ProductView.Attributes` hold only immutable IDs/slugs and product-specific values; the
handler fetches master `AttributeView`s (`attributeRepo.FindByIDs`) to resolve display names, option
labels, colors, and types, dropping any attribute whose master is missing or disabled. All four
query RPCs are **public** (no auth) — see `provideProcedurePermissions` in `connect/module.go`.

Filtering/faceting relies on the denormalized `attrs` map (`slug → value`) on each product, backed
by a **wildcard index** (`attrs.$**`, defined in `db/migrations/000001_init.up.json`). Facets are
computed in a single `$facet` aggregation; list filtering coerces string filter values to native
bool/numeric types for correct Mongo matching.

## Cross-cutting

- **Multi-tenancy is database-per-tenant.** Product/attribute views use
  `commonsmongo.NewGenericRepository` with `commonstenant.NewMultiTenantCollectionProvider`, which
  resolves `<base-db>_<tenant-slug>` from tenant context per request. When
  `multi-tenancy.enabled`, the commons tenant module applies migrations under `db/migrations/*.json`
  to every active tenant. Add index/schema changes there as numbered up/down JSON files; never
  hand-edit the collection.
- **Config**: `configs/config.standalone.yaml` (mongo, kafka consumers, `security.jwks`,
  observability), overridable by env/`.env`. Selected by `APP_ENV`.
- **Observability**: OpenTelemetry via `ecommerce-commons/pkg/observability`; tracing on, metrics off by
  default locally.
- **API contract is protobuf** and lives in the `-api` repo — regenerate there, never hand-edit
  generated Go/TS.

# AGENTS.md

## What this service is

`ecommerce-category-query-service` is the **CQRS read model for categories** in the
`ecommerce` workspace (see the workspace-root `AGENTS.md` one directory up for the multi-repo
shape, `go.work`, and cross-repo release-then-bump rules). It owns no writes: it projects
Kafka events emitted by the catalog service into its own per-tenant MongoDB collections and
serves them over Connect-RPC. Never make it call the catalog service synchronously for data
it should be projecting from events.

## Commands

```bash
make run                 # go run ./cmd/main.go
make build               # build bin/, injects VERSION via -ldflags
make test                # all tests, -race + coverage -> coverage.out
make test-unit           # -short only
make test-integration    # -tags=integration (real deps via testcontainers)
make lint                # golangci-lint (config .golangci.yml)
make fmt                 # gofmt -s + goimports
make generate-mocks      # mockery (v3) — no .mockery.yaml checked in yet; add one before use
make check-all           # deps + fmt + lint + test + vuln-check (mirrors CI)
```

CI is not local: `.github/workflows/*.yml` all `uses:` reusable workflows from
`ecommerce-infrastructure` (`go-ci.yml`, `go-release.yml`, `deploy.yml`). A push that changes
`VERSION` on `master` triggers release → deploy. `coverage-threshold: 0` there, so coverage is
not gated in CI even though `make test-coverage-check` exists locally.

## Architecture

**Hexagonal, wired with `go.uber.org/fx`.** `cmd/main.go` is the composition root: it only
assembles the commons, application, and infrastructure `fxconfig` modules — read it first. Do not
construct components in `main.go`.

Two aggregates live under `internal/application/`, and understanding why there are two is the
key to this service:

- **`categoryview/`** — the primary read model. A `CategoryView` stores only *immutable*
  attribute references + category-specific settings (role, sort order, filterable/searchable).
- **`attributeview/`** — *master data* for attributes (name, type, unit, options, enabled).
  Mutable attribute fields are deliberately **not** denormalized into `CategoryView`; they are
  joined at read time.

**Read-time join.** `connect/category_handler.go` fetches categories, collects their
`AttributeID`s, calls `attributeRepo.FindByIDs`, then `toProtoCategory` joins master data onto
each category attribute — dropping any attribute whose master record is missing or disabled.
This is intentional: attribute edits only touch `attributeview`, and every category reflects
them without reprojection.

**Inbound adapters** (`internal/infrastructure/inbound/`):
- `kafka/` — event consumers. `module.go` registers two consumer routers via
  `consumer.RegisterHandlerAndConsumer` (`category-events`, `attribute-events`); handlers map
  protobuf events (`catalog_eventsv1`) to domain views via `Reconstruct(...)` and call the
  upsert command handlers.
- `connect/` — the Connect-RPC / gRPC query API (`CategoryQueryService`).
  `provideProcedurePermissions` declares per-procedure auth (both read procedures are `nil` =
  public); handlers translate `mongo.ErrEntityNotFound` → `connect.CodeNotFound`.

**Outbound adapter** (`internal/infrastructure/outbound/mongo/`): repositories embed
`commonsmongo.GenericRepository[Domain, Entity]` and pair an `*_entity.go` + `*_mapper.go`.
Upserts go through `UpsertIfNewer` (version-based conflict resolution) — an out-of-order event

# AGENTS.md

## What this service is

`ecommerce-product-query-service` is the **read side of a CQRS split** for products. It owns no
writes to product data: it consumes domain events from Kafka (emitted by the catalog service and
image service) into its own denormalized MongoDB read model, and serves fast product queries over
Connect-RPC. **Never call the catalog service synchronously for data that should be projected from
events** — the projection is the source of truth for reads.

It is one repo inside a larger multi-repo workspace (see the parent `../AGENTS.md`). Its API
contract lives in the separate `ecommerce-product-query-service-api` repo; it consumes event
schemas from `ecommerce-catalog-service-api` and `ecommerce-image-service-api`. Locally these
resolve through the root `go.work`, so cross-repo changes are visible immediately without a
release/bump.

## Commands

```bash
make run                 # go run ./cmd/main.go
make build               # binary into bin/ (injects VERSION via -ldflags)
make test                # all tests, -race + coverage → coverage.out
make test-unit           # -short (unit only)
make test-integration    # -tags=integration (real deps)
make lint                # golangci-lint (config .golangci.yml)
make fmt                 # gofmt -s + goimports
make check-all           # deps + fmt + lint + test + vuln-check (the CI pipeline)
make install-tools       # golangci-lint, mockery, govulncheck, gosec, etc.
```

Run a single test: `go test ./internal/application/productview/ -run TestX -v`

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) delegates to the shared `ecommerce-infrastructure` Go CI workflow.

> Note: there are no `*_test.go` files in the repo yet.

## Architecture

**Hexagonal, wired entirely with `go.uber.org/fx`.** `cmd/main.go` is the composition root — it
only assembles the commons, application, and infrastructure `fxconfig` modules; no business logic
lives there. Do not construct components in `main.go`.

Two aggregates, each a folder under `internal/application/`:
- **`productview/`** — the product read model. Domain type `ProductView` is denormalized and
  read-optimized (unlike the command-side `Product`). Query handlers (`get_*.go`), command handlers
  (`upsert_product.go`, `delete_product.go`, `update_image_urls.go`), and the `Repository` port.
- **`attributeview/`** — master attribute definitions (name, type, options), projected separately
  and joined into products at query time.

### Layers
- `internal/application/<aggregate>/` — domain + use cases. `repository.go` is the port interface;
  handlers are split one-per-file and each defines its own `…QueryHandler` / `…CommandHandler`
  interface + constructor (registered in `application/module.go`).
- `internal/infrastructure/inbound/kafka/` — event consumers (the write path into the read model).
- `internal/infrastructure/inbound/connect/` — Connect-RPC handlers (the read path out).
- `internal/infrastructure/outbound/mongo/` — repository implementations (`*_entity.go` +
  `*_mapper.go` per aggregate).

### Event ingestion (the projection)
`kafka/module.go` registers two consumers via `consumer.RegisterHandlerAndConsumer` and routes each
event type to a handler method:
- `catalog-events` → `ProductUpdatedEvent`, `ProductDeletedEvent` (catalog),
  `ProductImagePromotedEvent` (image service).
- `catalog-attribute-events` → `AttributeUpdatedEvent`.

Two projection subtleties that must be preserved when editing the repo layer:
- **Version-guarded upsert** (`productViewRepository.Upsert`): the filter requires
  `version < event.Version`, so out-of-order/stale events are dropped (a matched/upserted count of 0
  is a logged no-op, not an error).
- **Image URLs are decoupled from product updates.** The image service publishes
  `ProductImagePromoted` only on promotion, not on every product change. `Upsert` therefore
  preserves existing `smallImageUrl`/`largeImageUrl` when `imageId` is unchanged (Mongo
  `$mergeObjects` pipeline), and `UpdateImageURLs` only writes when the stored `imageId` still
  matches — so an image event arriving before or after a product event never clobbers correct data.

### Read/query path
Connect handlers (`connect/product_handler.go`) translate proto ↔ domain and **join at read time**:
stored `ProductView.Attributes` hold only immutable IDs/slugs and product-specific values; the
handler fetches master `AttributeView`s (`attributeRepo.FindByIDs`) to resolve display names, option
labels, colors, and types, dropping any attribute whose master is missing or disabled. All four
query RPCs are **public** (no auth) — see `provideProcedurePermissions` in `connect/module.go`.

Filtering/faceting relies on the denormalized `attrs` map (`slug → value`) on each product, backed
by a **wildcard index** (`attrs.$**`, defined in `db/migrations/000001_init.up.json`). Facets are
computed in a single `$facet` aggregation; list filtering coerces string filter values to native
bool/numeric types for correct Mongo matching.

## Cross-cutting

- **Multi-tenancy is database-per-tenant.** Product/attribute views use
  `commonsmongo.NewGenericRepository` with `commonstenant.NewMultiTenantCollectionProvider`, which
  resolves `<base-db>_<tenant-slug>` from tenant context per request. When
  `multi-tenancy.enabled`, the commons tenant module applies migrations under `db/migrations/*.json`
  to every active tenant. Add index/schema changes there as numbered up/down JSON files; never
  hand-edit the collection.
- **Config**: `configs/config.standalone.yaml` (mongo, kafka consumers, `security.jwks`,
  observability), overridable by env/`.env`. Selected by `APP_ENV`.
- **Observability**: OpenTelemetry via `ecommerce-commons/pkg/observability`; tracing on, metrics off by
  default locally.
- **API contract is protobuf** and lives in the `-api` repo — regenerate there, never hand-edit
  generated Go/TS.

# AGENTS.md — ecommerce-tenant-service

Multi-tenancy service: source of truth for tenants, and the orchestrator for **self-service
tenant registration**. Consumed by every other service (each wires `tenant-service-api`).
Read the workspace-root `AGENTS.md` first for cross-repo rules (release-then-bump, hexagonal
layout, `fx` DI, `buf`-generated contracts, tenant conventions). This file covers what is
specific to *this* service.

## What this service does

Two distinct responsibilities live here:

1. **Tenant CRUD** (`internal/application/tenant/`) — plain command/query handlers over a Mongo
   `tenant` collection, emitting `TenantUpdatedEvent` / `TenantDeletedEvent` to Kafka via the
   transactional outbox. This is the read/write model other services project from.
2. **Registration saga** (`internal/application/registration/`) — a persistent, resumable saga
   that provisions a whole tenant from a signup: creates a Logto user, a tenant, assigns a role,
   publishes the tenant event, and triggers catalog seeding. This is the non-obvious core of the
   service — see below.

`cmd/main.go` is the composition root (fx modules only). Note the extra outbound adapters beyond
the usual Mongo/Kafka: `logto` (identity provider) and `k8s` (seeder job launcher).

## The registration saga (read this before touching `registration/`)

`Registration` (`registration.go`) is a persisted aggregate tracking saga progress with boolean
step flags (`TenantSet`, `RoleAssigned`, `EventPublished`, `CatalogSeeded`) and a `Status`
(`provisioning` → `completed`, or `compensating` → `rolled_back`).

- **Entry point** `register.go`: creates the Logto user *first* (synchronously), then persists the
  `Registration`, then attempts the saga **inline** (fast path). If any step fails inline, it
  returns with the registration still in-flight — the worker resumes it. Password is used once and
  discarded (never stored).
- **`processor.go`** runs steps forward (`Process`) and reverses them (`Compensate`). Every step is
  **idempotent**: it checks its flag/field and returns early if already done, so resuming a
  half-finished saga is safe. Each successful step is persisted immediately.
- **`worker.go`** polls every 10s (`FindActionable`) for registrations that are `provisioning` (with
  a due `NextRetryAt`) or `compensating`, and drives them forward or rolls them back. Registered as
  an fx `worker.RunWorker` in `application/module.go`.

Error handling rules — **preserve these when editing**:
- **Permanent errors** (`isPermanentError`: user/slug already exists, invalid data) → `MarkCompensating`,
  which triggers rollback. Transient errors → `ScheduleRetry` (exponential backoff, base 30s, cap 15m).
- **Catalog seeding never compensates.** It is non-critical: on failure it only schedules a retry.
  Do not add rollback for the seed step.
- Compensation deletes in reverse order (Logto user, then tenant) and is itself retryable.
- `completedAt` drives a Mongo TTL index (7 days) that reaps terminal registrations — do not repurpose
  that field.

## Outbound adapters specific to this service

- **`logto/`** — implements `tenant.IdentityProvider` against the Logto Management API over HTTP
  (OAuth2 client-credentials via `security.client-credentials`). Caches role IDs. `CreateUser`
  treats HTTP 409 as an existing-user conflict. Config key `logto.*` (`base-url`, `resource`,
  `client-id`, `client-secret`, `token-url`).
- **`k8s/`** — `SeederJobLauncher` implements `registration.CatalogSeeder` by cloning a **CronJob**
  template's job spec into a one-off Job (per-tenant, `GenerateName: seeder-<slug>-`). Uses
  `rest.InClusterConfig()`, so it only works when running inside the cluster. Config key `k8s.*`
  (`namespace`, `cronjob-name`).

## Ports & tests

Domain ports live in `internal/application/tenant/` (`Repository`, `IdentityProvider`,
`TenantEventFactory`) and `internal/application/registration/` (`Repository`, `CatalogSeeder`).
Implement new adapters against these; provide them through the relevant `fx` module, never
construct them in `main.go`.

There are currently no `*_test.go` files in this repo. The Makefile still exposes the standard
`test` / `test-unit` / `test-integration` (build tag `integration`) / `test-e2e` (tag `e2e`)
targets; follow the workspace testing conventions when adding tests.

## Config

YAML per env under `configs/` (`config.standalone.yaml`), overridable by env/`.env` (`APP_ENV`
selects the file). The standalone config does **not** include `logto` or `k8s` sections — those
are supplied by the deployment (Helm values) since the k8s seeder only runs in-cluster. Auth is
JWT via `security.jwks`; M2M calls to Logto use `security.client-credentials`.

## Storage

3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"strings"
6	
7		"github.com/knadh/koanf/parsers/yaml"

11	)

13	// NewKoanf creates a koanf instance loaded from the given config file and environment variables.
14	//
15	// Configuration is loaded in order (later overrides earlier):
16	//  1. YAML config file (if configFile is non-empty)
17	//  2. Environment variables
18	//
19	// Env convention: use __ (double underscore) as level delimiter, single _ as word separator.
20	//
21	//	OBSERVABILITY__OTEL_COLLECTOR_ENDPOINT → observability.otel-collector-endpoint
22	//	MONGO__MAX_POOL_SIZE                   → mongo.max-pool-size
23	//	LOGGER__LEVEL                          → logger.level
24	func NewKoanf(configFile string) (*koanf.Koanf, error) {
25		k := koanf.New(".")
26	
27		// 1. Load config file (if provided).
28		if configFile != "" {
29			if err := k.Load(file.Provider(configFile), yaml.Parser()); err != nil {
30				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read config file [%s]: %w", configFile, err)
31			}
32		}
33	
34		// 2. Load environment variables (overrides config file).
35		// Convention:
36		//   __ (double underscore) = level delimiter (becomes ".")
37		//   _  (single underscore) = word separator  (becomes "-")
38		//
39		// Examples:
40		//   OBSERVABILITY__OTEL_COLLECTOR_ENDPOINT → observability.otel-collector-endpoint
41		//   MONGO__CONNECTION_STRING               → mongo.connection-string
42		//   LOGGER__LEVEL                          → logger.level
43		//   APP_ENV                                → app-env
44		if err := k.Load(envprovider.Provider(".", envprovider.Opt{
45			TransformFunc: transformEnvKey,
46		}), nil); err != nil {
47			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to load environment variables: %w", err)
48		}
49	
50		return k, nil
51	}
52	
53	// transformEnvKey converts environment variable names to koanf key paths.
54	//
55	//	__ → . (level delimiter)
56	//	_  → - (word separator)
57	//
58	// All keys are lowercased.
59	func transformEnvKey(key, value string) (string, any) {
60		key = strings.ToLower(key)
61		// Replace __ first (level delimiter), then _ (word separator).
62		// Use a placeholder to avoid double replacement.
63		key = strings.ReplaceAll(key, "__", "\x00")
64		key = strings.ReplaceAll(key, "_", "-")
65		key = strings.ReplaceAll(key, "\x00", ".")
66		return key, value

# AGENTS.md

## What this is

`ecommerce-commons` is the shared Go library imported by every service in the ecommerce
workspace (catalog, product-query, category-query, image, tenant). It has **no `cmd/` and no
`main`**. It ships reusable building blocks plus their Fx wiring, which services compose in
their own `cmd/main.go`. There is nothing to "run"; you build, test, and lint it, and consumers
pick up changes locally through the root `go.work` (no tag/release needed for local dev — see the
workspace root `AGENTS.md`).

## Commands

```bash
make test                # all tests: -v -race -coverprofile
make test-unit           # -short (unit only)
make test-integration    # -tags=integration (spins up real deps via testcontainers — needs Docker)
make lint                # golangci-lint (v2; stricter-than-services config in .golangci.yml)
make fmt                 # gofmt -s + goimports
make generate-mocks      # mockery (not currently used)
make vuln-check          # govulncheck (excludes testutil/mocks/test)
make check-all           # deps + fmt + lint + test + vuln-check (the CI pipeline)
make install-tools       # golangci-lint, mockery, govulncheck, go-mod-outdated, go-licenses
```

Run a single test: `go test ./pkg/kafka/consumer/ -run TestRouter -v`
Integration tests are gated behind `-tags=integration`; plain `go test ./...` / `make test-unit` skips them.

## Module system (the core convention)

Runtime packages contain framework-agnostic functionality. Their Fx constructors and options
live in a sibling `fxconfig` package: for example, `pkg/mongo` is wired by
`pkg/mongo/fxconfig`, and configuration loading by `pkg/core/config/fxconfig`. Do not add Fx
imports or DI constructors to runtime packages. Add them to the closest `fxconfig` package.

Each Fx package exposes a constructor returning `fx.Option`, conventionally named
`New*Module()`. `pkg/fxconfig.NewCommonsModule()` aggregates the standard library modules:
core, HTTP, Mongo, observability, Kafka, tenant, client credentials, and JWKS validation.
Services can compose this aggregate or individual `fxconfig` modules; they do not construct
infrastructure components by hand.

Modules load their configuration from koanf through the shared configuration loader. Tests that
compose Fx modules must provide the required configuration through the normal configuration path.

Top-level modules and what they wire:
- `pkg/core/fxconfig` — `NewCoreModule()`: config loading (koanf + dotenv), zap logger, readiness
  health, and 5-minute Fx start/stop timeouts. This is the foundation every service starts with.
- `pkg/kafka/fxconfig` — `NewKafkaModule()`: Kafka configuration, producer, protobuf serde, and
  the outbox pattern. Consumer wiring is opt-in via `pkg/kafka/consumer/fxconfig`.
- `pkg/mongo/fxconfig` — `NewMongoModule()`: Mongo client, database, transaction manager, metric
  views, lifecycle, and the default single-database migration runner.
- `pkg/tenant/fxconfig` — `NewTenantModule()`: multi-tenancy lifecycle, migrations, cleanup worker,
  and Connect-RPC interceptors.
- `pkg/http/fxconfig`, `pkg/observability/fxconfig`, and `pkg/security/*/fxconfig` — transport,
  telemetry, and authentication building blocks.

Config loading is centralized in `config.Load[T]` (`pkg/core/config/loader.go`): each module loads
its own subtree of the service's YAML by key (`"mongo"`, `"kafka"`, etc.).

## Multi-tenancy (database-per-tenant)

Tenant data lives in a **separate Mongo database per tenant**, named `{baseDatabase}_{slug}`.
The slug is resolved per-request from context. This is the single most important cross-cutting
concern to get right in repository code:

- `mongo.NewGenericRepository[Domain, Entity](...)` accepts a `mongo.CollectionProvider`. The
  provider resolves a collection for the request context, so services can supply either a fixed
  collection or tenant-aware collection selection without changing repository code.
- `tenant.NewMultiTenantCollectionProvider(...)` — tenant-aware collection selection. It resolves
  the database from the tenant in request context and is required for tenant-scoped data.
- `mongo.NewStaticCollectionProvider(...)` — fixed collection in the base database, suitable for
  non-tenant data such as the transactional `outbox`.

Choosing the wrong provider silently reads/writes the wrong database, so match it to whether the
data is tenant-scoped. See `pkg/mongo/collection_provider.go` and
`generic_repository.go`.

## Connect-RPC interceptor ordering

Interceptors are collected via the fx group `connect_interceptor` and sorted by an integer
`Priority` (**lower runs earlier**). Because ordering is global across packages, the priorities
are coordinated constants — when adding an interceptor, pick a priority that fits this chain:

```
10 Recovery  15 Tracing  18 Tenant-Resolver  20 Logger  22 Auth
25 Validation  26 Tenant-Validator  30 Timeout  40 RateLimit  50 Bulkhead
```

The named constants live in `pkg/tenant/fxconfig/module.go`
(`ResolverInterceptorPriority=18`, `ValidatorInterceptorPriority=26`) and
`pkg/security/validation/fxconfig/module.go` (`AuthInterceptorPriority=22`). Tracing uses 15 in
`pkg/observability/fxconfig/module.go`; the built-in chain is in
`pkg/http/connect/interceptor/fxconfig/module.go`. Tenant/logger/auth ordering is deliberate:
resolve tenant before logging so the tenant field appears in logs, validate auth after logging so
failures are logged.

## Linting notes

`.golangci.yml` is intentionally strict for a library: `godot` (comments end with a period),
`revive`'s `exported` rule (exported symbols need doc comments), `gocyclo` at complexity 20,
plus `gosec` and `errcheck` with `check-blank`/`check-type-assertions`. Test files relax several
of these. Documentation comments are encouraged for exported symbols but are no longer enforced by CI.

# Plan: move Catalog Management from Redpanda to Apache Kafka

## Scope

The services `ecommerce-catalog-service` and `ecommerce-image-service` move to Kafka
(`kafka:29092`). The tenant, product-query and category-query services stay on Redpanda.
MirrorMaker 2 bridges the two brokers.

## What the evidence shows

**Producers (from source):**
- The catalog service produces `catalog.product.events`, `catalog.category.events` and
  `catalog.attribute.events` (`src/ecommerce-catalog-service-api/pkg/events/topics.go:11-21`).
- The image service produces `ProductImagePromotedEvent` to `catalog.product.events`
  (`src/ecommerce-image-service-api/pkg/events/topics.go:11-16`).
- The tenant service produces `tenant.tenant.events`
  (`src/ecommerce-tenant-service/internal/infrastructure/outbound/kafka/event_factory.go:19-42`).

**Consumers (source, plus the runtime group descriptions from R1):**

| Group (= service) | Topics on Redpanda |
|---|---|
| ecommerce-catalog-service | tenant.tenant.events |
| ecommerce-image-service | catalog.product.events, tenant.tenant.events |
| ecommerce-product-query-service | catalog.product.events, catalog.attribute.events, tenant.tenant.events |
| ecommerce-category-query-service | catalog.category.events, catalog.attribute.events, tenant.tenant.events |

All lags were 0 when R1 was taken. End offsets: product 120, category 4, attribute 20, tenant 1.

**Bindings that cross the boundary (q2):**
- Inbound (Redpanda → Kafka): catalog-service and image-service × `tenant.tenant.events`.
- Outbound (Kafka → Redpanda): product-query × `catalog.product.events` and
  `catalog.attribute.events`; category-query × `catalog.category.events` and
  `catalog.attribute.events`.

**Bindings that do not cross:**
- The image service on `catalog.product.events`: both producers of that topic move, so this
  stays inside Kafka.
- The query services on `tenant.tenant.events`: these stay on Redpanda.

## Design

Two MM2 flows run in one dedicated-mode MM2 process, in a new container `mm2-catalog`. It uses the
already-present `apache/kafka:4.1.2@sha256:5cc2a2fd…` image and runs
`/opt/kafka/bin/connect-mirror-maker.sh`.

| Flow | Topics |
|---|---|
| redpanda → kafka | `tenant.tenant.events` |
| kafka → redpanda | `catalog.product.events`, `catalog.category.events`, `catalog.attribute.events` |

The allow-lists are disjoint, so no topic is mirrored in both directions. Each topic has exactly
one "home" broker after the cutover:
- `catalog.*` lives on Kafka: all of their producers move.
- `tenant.*` lives on Redpanda: its producer stays.

**IdentityReplicationPolicy.** Services subscribe by exact topic name, and the default policy
would prefix topics (`redpanda.tenant.tenant.events`). The identity policy keeps the names, but it
removes MM2's own cycle protection, so the disjointness above is what keeps loops out. For the
same reason:
- Heartbeats are disabled on both flows. MM2 always replicates heartbeats topics, which under
  the identity policy would be a two-way mirror.
- The preflight checks that no `heartbeats` topic exists.

**Offsets:**
- On Kafka, the `catalog.*` topics are new and empty. The image service starts on them from
  offset 0 and sees only post-move events. No replay is needed.
- On Redpanda, mirrored `catalog.*` records are appended after the current end offsets, so the
  query groups continue where they are.
- For `tenant.tenant.events`, the moved groups would otherwise start from the beginning
  (`default-auto-offset-reset: earliest`) and re-run tenant migrations and cleanup. MM2
  checkpoints with `sync.group.offsets.enabled` are therefore turned on for redpanda→kafka only,
  limited to `ecommerce-catalog-service` and `ecommerce-image-service`.
- The plan checks the synced offsets before the services start. If they are wrong, it stops
  instead of resetting by hand.
- Checkpoints and offset sync are off for kafka→redpanda, so no Redpanda group is ever written.

**Topic config and ACL sync** are disabled, so MM2 doesn't change the existing Redpanda topics.

**Cutover order:**
1. Stop the catalog service first.
2. Let the image service drain its Redpanda backlog on `catalog.product.events`, then stop it.
3. Switch both services to `kafka:29092` and start them again.

Outbox rows that were not yet sent stay in MongoDB, and the relay sends them to Kafka after the
restart. The broker switch is a Helm-values change (`kafka.brokers`, or env `KAFKA__BROKERS`, see
`src/ecommerce-commons/pkg/core/config/koanf.go:19-24`). It is outside the workspace, so the
platform team makes it and applies it with helm, not Tilt.

## Steps (see plan.json)

| Step | What it does |
|---|---|
| P00 | Preflight gate: Kafka empty, topic configs, no heartbeats/mm2 topics, container name free, image present. Stop on any failure. |
| P01 | Create the four topics on Kafka with partitions and cleanup policy matching Redpanda. |
| P02 | Write `mm2/mm2-catalog.properties` (flows F1 and F2). |
| P03 | Start `mm2-catalog`; record the MM2 internal topics it creates. |
| P04 | Verify the inbound copy and the synced tenant offsets for the two moved groups. |
| P05 | Record replicas, stop the catalog service, drain the image service, stop it, record end offsets. |
| P06 | Platform team switches the brokers and scales both services back up. |
| P07 | Verify the groups are attached on the correct brokers. |
| P08 | `OPERATOR: please run the functional test`, plus checks that events flow end to end in both directions. Stop on failure. |
| P09 | Rollback path. |
| P10 | Cleanup scope: only what this plan created, checked by name first. |

## Things not established

The details are in answers.json q5. In short:
- Redpanda topic configs and Kafka emptiness were not available (R6).
- The Helm values were not available (R5): deployed group ids, DLQ settings and the broker key are
  unknown.
- R1 is a snapshot, so the seeder job, any stopped services and the UIs are not covered.
- Redpanda/MM2 behaviour and offset translation are not tested.

Nothing here claims the move is lossless or exactly-once. MM2 is at-least-once, and the
downstream projections tolerate duplicates only because they are version-guarded
(`product-update-flow.md:43-45`).
